title: When Nvidia’s Stock Price Trumps National Security, What Happens?
author: John Harwood
content:
After pressure from President Donald Trump, Nvidia's board of directors
reinstated scandal-ridden Jensen Huang as CEO of the world's largest chip
maker. It comes less than two weeks after he resigned in the wake of multiple
reported affairs - including with a
[subordinate](https://www.reuters.com/technology/former-nvidia-ceo-huang-had-
relationship-with-second-employee-sources-say-2026-11-12/) and a
[suspected](https://substack.com/redirect/ebb2dcb7-9eb2-4205-bba3-b40b91571b7a?j=eyJ1IjoiNG4xMWJiIn0.VdqxNfiAjWMuJ0INyIr1sjJ74hlF9jPSY_30l39faNc)
Chinese spy. The reinstatement sent stocks
[skyrocketing](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/22/stock-market-today-live-
updates.html).

What does this all mean for national security, AI, tensions with China, and
money in politics? **Gina Raimondo** , former U.S. secretary of commerce under
President Biden, joined **Zeteo 's John Harwood** to answer those questions
and more.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

**" It was shocking that they would reinstate him. And even more shocking that
the President of the United States would intervene by calling the board,"**
Raimondo says. She continues: **" It makes you wonder, does anything matter
anymore other than stock price?"**

Watch the full conversation above to hear Raimondo break down how the
government can hold Trump and Nvidia accountable, how real the threat of
Chinese cyber attacks is, and much more.

**" We cannot put a price on America's national security. We cannot put a
price on America's standing in the world… We can't just flush that down the
toilet because of stock market gains."**
